question: For how many years does the Indian Vice-President hold office?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vice-President of India holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office. (भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति का कार्यकाल — पाँच वर्ष)

• However, he continues to hold office beyond the five-year term until his successor assumes charge, and he is eligible for re-election any number of times.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India; Article 64 makes him the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

• He is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament (elected and nominated) by the system of proportional representation with a single transferable vote.

• Minimum age: 35 years; he must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• The Vice-President may resign by writing to the President and may be removed by a resolution passed by an effective majority of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha (Article 67(b)). The President of India also has a five-year term (Article 56).

question: Which among the following was the son of the Mughal emperor Shahjahan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurangzeb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aurangzeb was the son of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal. He won the war of succession (1657–58), imprisoned his father in the Agra Fort and ascended the throne in 1658 with the title Alamgir. (औरंगज़ेब — शाहजहाँ का पुत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shah Jahan's four sons were Dara Shikoh, Shah Shuja, Aurangzeb and Murad Baksh; Aurangzeb defeated all of them.

• Humayun was the son of Babur; Jahangir was the son of Akbar and the father of Shah Jahan.

• Sikandar Lodi belonged to the Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, not to the Mughals.

NOTE

• Mughal succession: Babur (1526) → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb (d. 1707). Shah Jahan's reign is called the Golden Age of Mughal architecture (Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid).

question: Who popularised the 'Pandanallur Style' in Bharatanatyam and received Padma Bhushan in 2004?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alarmel Valli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alarmel Valli is the celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer who popularised the Pandanallur style (bani) of Bharatanatyam and was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2004. (अलार्मेल वल्ली — पंडनल्लूर शैली)

• She trained under the legendary guru Chokkalingam Pillai and his son Subbaraya Pillai of the Pandanallur lineage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni; its major styles (banis) are Pandanallur, Vazhuvoor, Thanjavur, Melattur and Kalakshetra.

• Mallika Sarabhai (daughter of Vikram Sarabhai and Mrinalini Sarabhai) is known for Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi; Kumari Kamala was a noted dancer-actress; Madhuri Dixit is a film actress trained in Kathak.

NOTE

• Other celebrated Bharatanatyam exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra), Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam and Sonal Mansingh.

question: Which type of friction is considered as a self-adjusting force?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Static Friction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Static friction is called a self-adjusting force because it automatically adjusts its magnitude to be equal and opposite to the applied force, up to a maximum value (the limiting friction), so long as the body does not move. (स्थैतिक घर्षण — स्वतः समायोजी बल)

◦ If you push a heavy box with 10 N and it does not move, static friction is exactly 10 N; push with 20 N and it becomes 20 N — until the limiting value is exceeded and the body slides.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kinetic (sliding) friction acts when a body is already sliding and has a nearly constant value (f = μₖN), so it is not self-adjusting.

• Rolling friction acts when a body rolls over a surface and is the smallest of the three, which is why wheels and ball bearings are used.

• There is no such force as "centripetal friction"; centripetal force is the net inward force needed for circular motion.

NOTE

• Order of magnitude: static (limiting) > kinetic > rolling. Friction is independent of the area of contact and depends on the normal reaction (N) and the nature of surfaces (μ). Friction is a necessary evil — it enables walking and braking but wastes energy as heat.

question: Alluri Sitaram Raju was a tribal freedom fighter from state ______ of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alluri Sitarama Raju was a tribal freedom fighter from the Andhra Pradesh region (the Visakhapatnam agency area of the then Madras Presidency). He led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 against the British. (अल्लूरी सीताराम राजू — आंध्र प्रदेश)

• He is popularly called "Manyam Veerudu" (Hero of the Jungle) and was killed by the British in 1924.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Rampa (Manyam) Rebellion was triggered by the Madras Forest Act of 1882, which restricted the tribals' traditional podu (shifting) cultivation and access to forests.

• In 2022, the Government of India celebrated his 125th birth anniversary as part of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav, and a statue was unveiled at Bhimavaram.

NOTE

• Other major tribal uprisings: Santhal Hul (1855–56) — Sidhu and Kanhu; Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900) — Birsa Munda (Jharkhand); Kol Rebellion (1831); Bhil Revolt; Tana Bhagat Movement.

question: SAI is the apex national sports body of India. What is the full form of SAI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sports Authority of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SAI stands for the "Sports Authority of India", the apex national sports body of India under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. (भारतीय खेल प्राधिकरण)

• It was set up in 1984 to utilise the infrastructure created for the 1982 Asian Games held in Delhi, and its headquarters is at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, New Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• SAI runs talent-scouting and training schemes such as the National Centres of Excellence (NCOE), Khelo India centres, SAI Training Centres (STC) and the Special Area Games (SAG) scheme.

• It also manages major stadia in Delhi such as the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium and the SPM Swimming Complex.

NOTE

• Related bodies: IOA (Indian Olympic Association), NADA (National Anti-Doping Agency), LNIPE (Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education, Gwalior) and the NSNIS, Patiala (Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports).

question: Who among the following was a Shaka ruler in India (AD 130-150)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudradaman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rudradaman I (c. AD 130–150) was the most famous Shaka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler of India, belonging to the Kardamaka dynasty with his capital at Ujjain. (रुद्रदामन प्रथम — शक शासक)

• He is celebrated for the Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription of c. AD 150 — the first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit — which records his repair of the Sudarshana Lake, originally built during Chandragupta Maurya's reign and improved by Ashoka.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chashtana was indeed an earlier Western Kshatrapa ruler and the grandfather of Rudradaman, but the specific period AD 130–150 belongs to Rudradaman.

• Bindusara was the Mauryan emperor (son of Chandragupta Maurya, father of Ashoka), not a Shaka.

NOTE

• The Shakas (Scythians) entered India through the north-west in the 1st century BCE. Vikramaditya of Ujjain is traditionally said to have defeated them in 58 BCE, marking the start of the Vikrama Samvat. The Saka Era (78 CE), India's national calendar, is associated with Kanishka.

question: Sam has an income of 9 lakh rupees yearly. Which tax slab (new regime) of India is applicable for him as per the new regime Income Tax Slab Rates FY 2021-22?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the new (concessional) income-tax regime introduced by Section 115BAC for FY 2021-22, the slab of ₹7,50,001 to ₹10,00,000 attracted a tax rate of 15%. Since Sam's annual income is ₹9 lakh, the applicable slab rate is 15%. (नई कर व्यवस्था — 15% स्लैब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• New regime slabs for FY 2021-22: up to ₹2.5 lakh — Nil; ₹2.5–5 lakh — 5%; ₹5–7.5 lakh — 10%; ₹7.5–10 lakh — 15%; ₹10–12.5 lakh — 20%; ₹12.5–15 lakh — 25%; above ₹15 lakh — 30%.

• The new regime offers lower rates but no major exemptions/deductions (such as 80C, 80D, HRA and LTA), whereas the old regime keeps higher rates with deductions.

NOTE

• Income tax is a direct tax levied by the Central Government and administered by the CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes) under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. Direct taxes cannot be shifted to another person, unlike indirect taxes such as GST.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution talks about a uniform civil code?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 44.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 44 of the Constitution states that "the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout the territory of India". (अनुच्छेद 44 — समान नागरिक संहिता)

• It falls under Part IV — the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are non-justiciable (not enforceable by any court) but fundamental in the governance of the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 352 — proclamation of National Emergency (war, external aggression or armed rebellion).

• Article 14 — Right to Equality (equality before law and equal protection of the laws).

• Article 370 — the temporary special status of Jammu and Kashmir, abrogated in August 2019.

NOTE

• Goa has long had a common civil code (the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867), and Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to pass a UCC Bill (2024). Other important DPSPs: Article 39A (free legal aid), Article 40 (panchayats), Article 43 (living wage), Article 48A (environment protection).

question: Ustad Bismillah Khan was one of the greatest exponents of the ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehnai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) was the greatest exponent of the "Shehnai", a double-reed wind instrument. He is credited with bringing the shehnai — earlier confined to weddings and temple processions — onto the classical concert stage. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खाँ — शहनाई)

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, becoming the third classical musician to receive it.

• He famously played the shehnai from the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, India's first Independence Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Flute (Bansuri) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh.

• Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Alla Rakha, Pandit Kishan Maharaj.

• Sitar — Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tat/Tantu Vadya (string — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushir Vadya (wind — shehnai, flute), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam), Ghan Vadya (solid percussion — manjira, jaltarang).

question: According to census 2011, percentage of Urban population in India is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31.16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, about 31.16% of India's population lived in urban areas (approximately 37.7 crore people), while about 68.84% lived in rural areas. (जनगणना 2011 — शहरी जनसंख्या 31.16%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 key figures: total population 121.09 crore; sex ratio 943 females per 1000 males; literacy rate 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%); density 382 persons per sq km; decadal growth 17.7%.

• Most urbanised state: Goa (62.2%); most urbanised UT: Delhi (97.5%); least urbanised state: Himachal Pradesh (10%).

• Most populous state: Uttar Pradesh; least populous: Sikkim.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The first synchronous census was held in 1881 under W. C. Plowden. Census 2011 was the 15th national census.

question: The Bhagirathi river originates from Gaumukh Glacier. It meets the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form river ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ganga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhagirathi, which originates from the Gaumukh snout of the Gangotri glacier (Uttarakhand), meets the Alaknanda at Devprayag, and from this confluence the river is known as the Ganga. (देवप्रयाग — भागीरथी + अलकनंदा = गंगा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Panch Prayag (five confluences) of Uttarakhand: Vishnuprayag (Alaknanda + Dhauliganga), Nandprayag (Alaknanda + Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Alaknanda + Pindar), Rudraprayag (Alaknanda + Mandakini) and Devprayag (Alaknanda + Bhagirathi).

• The Ganga is about 2,525 km long — India's longest river — and drains the largest river basin in the country.

• Major left-bank tributaries: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi; right-bank: Yamuna, Son.

NOTE

• The Ganga was declared the National River of India in 2008. In Bangladesh it is called the Padma, and after joining the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) and Meghna it forms the Sundarbans delta, the world's largest delta.

question: Name the brand under which all the fertilizers will be sold under the "One Nation One Fertilizer" scheme launched by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the "One Nation One Fertilizer" scheme (formally the Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janurvarak Pariyojana — PMBJP), launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2022, all subsidised fertilizers are sold under the single brand name "Bharat". (एक राष्ट्र एक उर्वरक — भारत ब्रांड)

◦ Thus urea is sold as "Bharat Urea", DAP as "Bharat DAP", MOP as "Bharat MOP" and NPK as "Bharat NPK", irrespective of the manufacturing company.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The scheme is implemented by the Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

• Two-thirds of the fertilizer bag now carries the Bharat brand and the PMBJP logo, while the company's own name and logo are limited to one-third of the space.

• Aims: to end brand-based confusion, curb criss-cross movement of fertilizers and reduce high freight subsidy costs.

NOTE

• It was launched along with the PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras (PMKSK) — one-stop shops for seeds, fertilizers, soil testing and farm advisory services.

question: Gangaur is an Indian festival majorly celebrated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gangaur" is a colourful festival celebrated mainly in Rajasthan (and parts of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Braj) in the month of Chaitra (March–April). It is dedicated to Gauri (Parvati) and Isar (Shiva). (गणगौर — राजस्थान)

• The name comes from "Gan" (Shiva) + "Gaur" (Gauri/Parvati). Unmarried girls pray for a good husband and married women for the long life and well-being of their husbands.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The festival begins the day after Holi and lasts for 18 days, culminating in grand processions of the images of Gauri, especially in Jaipur, Udaipur, Bikaner and Jodhpur.

• Other important Rajasthani festivals/fairs: Teej, Pushkar Camel Fair, Desert Festival (Jaisalmer), Marwar Festival, Kajli Teej (Bundi).

NOTE

• Festival-state matching for SSC: Bihu — Assam; Onam & Vishu — Kerala; Pongal — Tamil Nadu; Baisakhi — Punjab; Losar — Ladakh/Himachal; Hornbill — Nagaland; Bhagoria — Madhya Pradesh; Gangaur & Teej — Rajasthan.

question: ______ is the division of the cytoplasm of one eukaryotic cell into two daughter cells.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cytokinesis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cytokinesis" is the division of the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell that follows nuclear division and results in two separate daughter cells. (कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन)

◦ In animal cells it occurs by the furrowing/constriction of the plasma membrane; in plant cells it occurs by the formation of a cell plate from the centre outwards.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Karyokinesis" is the division of the nucleus, which takes place in four stages — prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase — and normally precedes cytokinesis.

• "Sepsis" is a life-threatening medical condition caused by the body's extreme response to infection; "Genesis" means origin or beginning. Both are unrelated to cell division.

NOTE

• Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells and is used for growth and repair; Meiosis produces four haploid gametes and provides variation. In some cases karyokinesis occurs without cytokinesis, producing multinucleate (coenocytic) cells.

question: The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 belongs to ______ Ministry of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Earth Sciences.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 was introduced and piloted by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). It was passed by Parliament in 2022 and became the Antarctic Act, 2022. (भारतीय अंटार्कटिक विधेयक, 2022 — पृथ्वी विज्ञान मंत्रालय)

• The Act gives effect to India's obligations under the Antarctic Treaty, the Protocol on Environmental Protection (Madrid Protocol) and the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It provides for a Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection, requires a permit for Indian expeditions to Antarctica, prohibits mining and nuclear activity there, and extends Indian jurisdiction over Indian citizens in Antarctica.

• India's Antarctic research stations: Dakshin Gangotri (1983, now decommissioned), Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012). India's Arctic station is Himadri (2008) at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard.

• The nodal agency for polar research is the NCPOR (National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research), Goa, under MoES.

NOTE

• India signed the Antarctic Treaty in 1983 and became a Consultative Party the same year. The Antarctic Treaty (1959, in force 1961) reserves Antarctica for peaceful and scientific purposes.

question: Which city hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beijing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The XXIV Olympic Winter Games (2022) were hosted by Beijing, China, from 4 to 20 February 2022. (बीजिंग — शीतकालीन ओलंपिक 2022)

• Beijing thus became the first city in history to host both the Summer Olympics (2008) and the Winter Olympics (2022).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mascot: Bing Dwen Dwen (a panda); motto: "Together for a Shared Future".

• Norway topped the medal tally with 16 golds. India was represented by a single athlete, the alpine skier Arif Khan.

• Tokyo hosted the Summer Olympics 2020 (held in 2021); Milan-Cortina d'Ampezzo (Italy) will host the Winter Olympics 2026; Melbourne hosted the Summer Olympics in 1956.

NOTE

• Upcoming Olympics: Paris 2024 (Summer), Milan-Cortina 2026 (Winter), Los Angeles 2028 (Summer), Brisbane 2032 (Summer). The Winter Olympics began at Chamonix, France, in 1924.

question: Which Indian state is home to the Buddhist cave temples known as Barabar Caves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Barabar Caves, situated in the Jehanabad district of Bihar (about 24 km north of Gaya), are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating from the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE). (बराबर की गुफाएँ — बिहार)

• They were excavated during the reigns of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha Maurya and were donated to the Ajivika sect (with later Buddhist and Jain associations).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Famous caves in the group: Lomas Rishi (noted for its arch-shaped facade imitating wooden architecture), Sudama, Karan Chaupar and Vishwakarma; the nearby Nagarjuni hills contain the Gopika, Vadathika and Vapiya caves.

• The interiors are famous for the Mauryan polish — an extraordinarily smooth, mirror-like finish on the granite walls.

• The caves inspired the "Marabar Caves" in E. M. Forster's novel A Passage to India.

NOTE

• Other important cave sites: Ajanta, Ellora, Elephanta, Karla, Bhaja, Kanheri (Maharashtra), Udayagiri–Khandagiri (Odisha) and Bagh (Madhya Pradesh).

question: Which state is the leading producer of sugar in India, as of May 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of May 2022, Maharashtra was the leading producer of sugar in India, having overtaken Uttar Pradesh in sugar output. (महाराष्ट्र — चीनी उत्पादन में अग्रणी)

• Maharashtra's sugar industry is concentrated in the Ahmednagar, Kolhapur, Solapur, Pune and Satara districts and is dominated by cooperative sugar mills.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh remains the largest producer of sugarcane (the raw crop), while Maharashtra has led in sugar (the processed product) in recent seasons owing to higher recovery rates.

• India is the world's largest consumer of sugar and among the largest producers, along with Brazil.

• Sugarcane is a tropical/kharif cash crop needing 21–27°C temperature and 75–150 cm rainfall.

NOTE

• The sugar industry is India's second largest agro-based industry after textiles. Sugarcane by-products: bagasse (fuel/paper), molasses (alcohol/ethanol) and press mud (fertilizer). Ethanol blending with petrol is a major current policy push.

question: Which freedom fighter of India led the famous revolt of 1857 (sepoy mutiny) at Lucknow?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Begum Hazrat Mahal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Begum Hazrat Mahal, the wife of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh, led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow. She proclaimed her young son Birjis Qadr as the ruler of Awadh and organised resistance against the British. (बेगम हज़रत महल — लखनऊ, 1857)

• After the fall of Lucknow she retreated and finally took refuge in Nepal, where she died in 1879.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Centres and leaders of the Revolt of 1857: Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar & General Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb & Tatya Tope; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Bihar (Jagdishpur) — Kunwar Singh; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah.

• The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, triggered by the greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle; Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore was among the first to rebel.

NOTE

• Consequences: the Government of India Act, 1858 ended Company rule; India came under the direct rule of the British Crown, and Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858) promised non-interference in religious matters. Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and first Viceroy.

question: Pandit Lachhu Maharaj was primarily associated to which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Lachhu Maharaj (1907–1978) was a legendary exponent and choreographer of the "Kathak" classical dance form, belonging to the famous Lucknow gharana of Kathak. (पंडित लच्छू महाराज — कथक)

• He choreographed dance sequences for classic Hindi films such as Mughal-e-Azam, Pakeezah and Mahal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); the word derives from "Katha" (story) — the kathakars narrated stories through dance. It is noted for fast footwork (tatkar), chakkars (spins) and intricate rhythmic patterns.

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow (grace and expression — Bindadin Maharaj, Birju Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj), Jaipur (footwork and technique) and Banaras.

• Other Kathak greats: Pandit Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Gopi Krishna.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: The Windvane instrument measures the ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is wind-direction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "wind vane (weather vane)" is the instrument used to measure/indicate the direction of the wind. It consists of a freely rotating arrow-shaped pointer that turns so that its head points into the wind, i.e., towards the direction from which the wind is blowing. (पवन दिशा सूचक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Anemometer — measures wind speed/velocity.

• Hygrometer — measures relative humidity; a wet-and-dry-bulb hygrometer is called a psychrometer.

• Thermometer — measures temperature; Barometer — measures atmospheric pressure; Rain gauge — measures rainfall.

NOTE

• Winds are always named after the direction from which they blow — a "westerly" blows from the west. Other instruments for SSC: seismograph (earthquakes), lactometer (purity of milk), hydrometer (relative density of liquids), altimeter (altitude), odometer (distance travelled).

question: National Family Benefit Scheme was started in August ______ by Government of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS)" was launched on 15 August 1995 as one of the components of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP). (राष्ट्रीय परिवार लाभ योजना — 1995)

• It provides a lump-sum cash assistance to a BPL household on the death of its primary breadwinner (aged 18–59 years). The amount, initially ₹5,000 (₹10,000 for accidental death), was later revised to ₹20,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The NSAP (launched 15 August 1995) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development giving effect to Article 41 of the Constitution (right to public assistance in cases of old age, sickness and disablement).

• NSAP components: IGNOAPS (old-age pension), IGNWPS (widow pension), IGNDPS (disability pension), NFBS (family benefit) and the Annapurna Scheme (free foodgrains to uncovered destitute elderly).

NOTE

• Other schemes launched in 1995: the Mid-Day Meal Scheme (15 August 1995) and the Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana context reforms. NFBS assistance is now generally paid through DBT into the beneficiary's bank account.

question: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an ecosystem is called ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is stratification.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stratification" is the vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels (strata) in an ecosystem. (स्तरण)

◦ Example: In a forest, trees occupy the top layer (canopy), shrubs the middle layer and herbs/grasses the bottom layer; below that lie the litter and soil layers.

• Stratification allows many species to coexist by reducing direct competition for light and space — an aspect of niche differentiation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Biomagnification" is the increase in the concentration of a non-degradable pollutant (e.g., DDT, mercury) at successively higher trophic levels of a food chain.

• "Coevolution" is the reciprocal evolutionary change in interacting species (e.g., flowers and their pollinators).

• "Decomposition" is the breakdown of complex dead organic matter into inorganic substances by decomposers such as bacteria and fungi.

NOTE

• Steps of decomposition: fragmentation → leaching → catabolism → humification → mineralisation. Other ecosystem attributes: productivity, energy flow, nutrient cycling and stratification. Aquatic ecosystems show stratification too — the littoral, limnetic, profundal and benthic zones.
